newsitem.title: UK: UK has always backed Japanese car firms in EU-Lang.
newsitem.headline: UK has always backed Japanese car firms in EU-Lang.

text.p: Trade Secretary Ian Lang, reacting to reports from Tokyo that Toyota could switch its investment to the continent if Britain stays out of Europe's single currency, said on Wednesday the government had always stood up for Japanese carmakers based in Britain.

"The British government consistently backed the Japanese car industry in the single market to ensure that Japanese cars built in the United Kingdom have no restrictions placed on them within the European Union," Lang said in a statement.
He said Toyota as well as Honda and Nissan had all recently announced plans to expand their investments in Britain.

In a statement aimed at reassuring Japanese businessmen, Lang added: "No decision on economic and monetary union has been taken. We have made it quite clear that we will not make this decision until we know all the facts.
"A number of Japnese businessmen have expressed concern about the potential stability of a single currency."
Lang paid tribute to the huge influx of Japanese inward investment in Britain. He said it revolutionised Britain's car industry and its supply chain in the past decade.
